graph.summary: Isoniazid → InhA → mycolic acid biosynthetic process → Mycobacterium tuberculosis → Pulmonary Tuberculosis

evidence.snippet: A reactive form of isoniazid inhibits InhA by reacting with the NAD(H) cofactor bound to the enzyme active site forming a covalent adduct (isonicotinic acyl NADH) that is apt to bind with high affinity.
evidence.explanation: Isoniazid is a prodrug activated by the mycobacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG; the resulting isonicotinoyl-NAD adduct inhibits InhA (enoyl-ACP reductase).

paper.title: Mechanisms for isoniazid action and resistance.

evidence.snippet: This isonicotinyl-NAD adduct inhibits the activity of 2-trans-enoyl-ACP(CoA) reductase (InhA), which plays a role in mycolic acid biosynthesis.

paper.title: Is IQG-607 a Potential Metallodrug or Metallopro-Drug With a Defined Molecular Target in Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

evidence.snippet: InhA, an essential enzyme of the mycolic acid biosynthetic pathway and the primary target of the anti-tubercular drug isoniazid
evidence.explanation: InhA is an enoyl-ACP reductase essential for the mycolic acid biosynthetic pathway.

paper.title: Phosphorylation of InhA inhibits mycolic acid biosynthesis and growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

evidence.snippet: InhA is a member of the mycobacterial Type II fatty acid biosynthesis system, which elongates acyl fatty acid precursors of mycolic acids.

paper.title: Slow-onset inhibition of 2-trans-enoyl-ACP (CoA) reductase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis by an inorganic complex.

evidence.snippet: Mycobacterium tuberculosis has a complex cell wall containing mycolic acids (MA), which play an important role in pathogenesis, virulence, and survival by protecting the cell against harsh environments.
evidence.explanation: Mycolic acid biosynthesis is an essential process unique to Mycobacterium tuberculosis; disrupting it kills the bacterium.

paper.title: Genomic characterization of variants on mycolic acid metabolism genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Santa Catarina, Southern Brazil.
paper.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases

evidence.snippet: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of mortality due to a bacterial pathogen, Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
evidence.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the causative agent of tuberculosis, including pulmonary tuberculosis.

paper.title: Slow-onset inhibition of 2-trans-enoyl-ACP (CoA) reductase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis by an inorganic complex.
